name: DEAP-3600
full_name: Dark matter Experiment using Argon Pulse-shape discrimination
summary: DEAP-3600 uses a large single-phase liquid-argon target at SNOLAB to search for dark matter through scintillation timing. DEAP-1 was its technological predecessor.
detection_principle: Nuclear and electron recoils produce different liquid-argon scintillation time profiles. An array of photodetectors records light yield, timing and position for pulse-shape discrimination and rejection of surface backgrounds.

results.summary: No candidates were observed in the WIMP search window; upper limits on spin-independent scattering were obtained with a liquid-argon target.

science_scope: This record covers experiments that directly measure possible interactions between dark matter and ordinary matter. Published exclusion limits, background events and projected sensitivities do not constitute a dark-matter discovery.
